Mill bridge reopens after two years

The footbridge over the river by the old mill opened again on Saturday morning after two years of repairs.

Engineers replaced the rusted iron frame and the wooden deck, and the council said the work came in under budget.

About two hundred people walked across in the first hour, many of them children on their way to the Saturday market.

The bridge was closed in the winter of the floods, when a survey found cracks in two of the four iron beams.

A temporary crossing downstream added twenty minutes to the walk into town for families on the east bank.

The new deck is made of larch from a forest in the next valley, chosen because it weathers well without treatment.

Lamps along the rail run on a small solar panel, and they come on at dusk and dim after midnight.

The mill itself, now a cafe and a small museum, will open late on Saturday evenings through the summer.

Correction panel: an earlier version of this story gave the wrong date for the opening of the cafe and the name of the engineer who led the survey of the iron beams.

Correction panel: the lamps were paid for by the bridge trust, not by the council, as an earlier version said in its second paragraph.
